eva: quick follow-up from the kernel selection + attention optim thread — found a couple of nasty interactions when KV is segmented/paged and the fused attention kernels expect contiguous KV windows.
sam: TL;DR?
eva: fused kernels assume contiguous per-head KV buffers. our pager produces noncontiguous segments after eviction + compaction -> kernels either have to gather into a temp buffer (extra copy) or support scatter/gather descriptors.
raj: yeah that will blow the fast path. kernels do a single cudaMemcpy + tuned loads. scattered pages break vectorized access patterns and prefetch heuristics.
julie: can we present an SG descriptor instead of copying? kernel could support two modes: CONTIGUOUS (fast) or SG (gather).
eva: prototype descriptor i sketched:
```c
// simple page map descriptor
struct KVPageEntry {
  uint64_t page_id;
  uint64_t gpu_addr; // 0 if not resident
  uint32_t bytes;
  uint8_t  resident;
};
// kernel receives array of KVPageEntry for each head window
```
sam: any perf numbers on SG vs contig?
eva: microbench on A100: SG path ~1.2-1.6x slower for short sequences (<=256). for long seqs the overhead amortizes, but SG causes less memory churn under high eviction rates.
raj: tradeoffs: SG avoids extra copy and reduces PCIe traffic when only a few pages are hot. but it increases kernel complexity and can hurt L2/cache behavior.
julie: what about fragmentation and compaction policies? we could run an async defrag when fragmentation > threshold, or compact aggressively on background.
eva: agreed. my concerns: 1) defrag is expensive and may conflict with realtime SLOs, 2) locking/consistency while kernel reads page map.
raj: propose RCU-style epoch pinning: kernel pins the current page snapshot, pager can schedule async compaction for pages not pinned. kernel pin/unpin calls are cheap.
sam: pin semantics need to be explicit. kernels should call pin() for the duration of token generation for a request. otherwise pager must fallback to copying.
julie: concurrency -> if the pager blocks to make a page resident we'll get stalls. prefetch policy + coalescing loads could reduce blocking. also add a medium-priority prefetch daemon.
eva: fallback strategies: a) SG-capable kernel path (works with noncontig) b) copy-into-contig buffer (slower but simpler) c) route to a different kernel variant that uses per-token gather (very slow) d) CPU fallback for extreme fragmentation.
sam: we should quantify break-even points and add them to the optimizer so routing can pick the best kernel per request.
raj: action items: I'll draft kernel API: pin/unpin + accept SG descriptor + hint flags (prefetch_ok, allow_copy). and add compatibility shim for older kernels to accept a synthesized contig buffer.
eva: i'll add an eviction simulator to perf infra to drive realistic fragmentation patterns (LRU, generational, size-tiered). need metrics: %fragmented windows, average resident pages per window, copy bytes/sec.
julie: i'll own the scheduler side: defrag policy + prefetch daemon + thresholds. also add a test that forces fragmentation >70% to validate fallback behavior.
sam: i'll run perf scenarios and collect latency/P99/cost delta for SG vs contig vs copy.
build-bot: CI: rfc-seg-compat branch built, unit tests green for the HDL kernel stubs.
eva: next sync: 30m on Wed to align on pin API and perf targets. please add items to the PR checklist: API doc, microbench harness, simulator, kernel shim.
julie: noted. thanks all :thumbsup:
sam: ack :eyes:
raj: sounds good. starting the kernel stub now.
